shipped_rows.title_o: Drones and Support for the Use of Force

blind_target.evidence_quote: To address this, we replicate and extend the research design of Walsh and Schulzke across three survey experiments.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We find that support for military action does not differ across treatments in which subjects are told that the attack involves drone strikes or ground troops.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract states that the prior finding was greater support with drones and reports no corresponding support difference in the replication experiments.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract explicitly says the authors replicate and extend Walsh and Schulzke's research design, and the only supplied shipped original is Walsh and Schulzke (2018). However, the source and supplied citation do not provide the original finding's title/year or enough detail to determine whether the new experiments retest that specific finding versus only reuse the design while addressing endogeneity. Full text and reference identity are needed.
luna_triage.location: Abstract only; source has no Results/References
luna_triage.omission_quote: To address this, we replicate and extend the research design of Walsh and Schulzke across three survey experiments.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Existing research finds that weapons that eliminate the possibility of military casualties, such as drones, increase popular support for engaging in conflict.

quality_gate: Luna is triage only. Independently establish actual empirical retesting and absence under ALL shipped identities/alternate reports. Read prior objections. No paper outcome is being requested.
